svg.title: The write path, with the human confirmation on the line rather than beside it
svg.desc: A single column of stages runs down the middle of the sketch, from an incoming tools/call for write_database to a committed transaction, with an arrow between every pair and no way around any of them. The stages in order are the deployment switch writes_enabled, the SQL validator, a dry-run check, a human reading the validated statement over a multi round-trip exchange, and one transaction that runs BEGIN, the statement, the audit insert and COMMIT. The three server-side checks are outlined in terracotta, the human gate is filled solid blue because it is the only stage that spends a person's attention, and the transaction is outlined in green. A dashed arrow leaves each stage to the left into an exit box naming the status the tool returns: disabled, rejected, dry_run, declined, and failed. Annotations on the right note that the switch is off by default so the write pool is never opened, that only INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE with a WHERE clause survive the validator, that nobody has been asked anything at any of the first three stages, that the confirmation shows the exact statement and that the approval parameter is stripped from the published input schema, and that the audit row is inserted on the same connection inside the same transaction so both land or neither does.
svg.text: The write path. Every gate is on the line.
Nothing routes around a stage. Each of the five exits on the left is a status the tool returns.
Off by default. With it off the
write pool is never even opened.
WHERE is required. No DDL, no
yet. Consent is spent only where
The audit row is inserted on this
Gates 1, 2 and the dry run all return without asking. Only gate 3 spends a person's attention, which is what keeps it worth something.
